argv:
Rewrite the text following the rules of The Elements of Style.

Omit needless words. Every word must tell. Use the active voice. Put
statements in positive form: say what something is, not what it is not.

Use definite, specific, concrete language in preference to the vague and
abstract. Keep related words together. Express coordinate ideas in parallel
form. Place the emphatic words of a sentence at the end.

Make the paragraph the unit of composition, each with a clear topic sentence.
Write with nouns and verbs rather than adjectives and adverbs. Avoid
qualifiers such as "rather", "very", and "little".

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
It is interesting to contemplate an entangled bank, clothed with many plants of many kinds, with birds singing on the bushes, with various insects flitting about, and with worms crawling through the damp earth, and to reflect that these elaborately constructed forms, so different from each other, and dependent on each other in so complex a manner, have all been produced by laws acting around us. These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms. Thus, from the war of nature, from famine and death, the most exalted object which we are capable of conceiving, namely, the production of the higher animals, directly follows. There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
</passage>

response.text:
Consider an entangled bank: plants of many kinds clothe it, birds sing in the bushes, insects flit about, and worms crawl through the damp earth. These forms, so different from each other, depend on each other in complex ways, yet laws acting around us have produced them all. State these laws broadly: Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance, which reproduction nearly implies; Variability, arising from the direct and indirect action of external conditions and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high that it forces a Struggle for Life, which in turn produces Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms.

Thus the war of nature, famine, and death directly produce the most exalted object we can conceive: the higher animals. This view of life holds grandeur. Its several powers were breathed originally into a few forms, or into one; and while this planet has cycled on according to the fixed law of gravity, endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have evolved, and continue to evolve, from so simple a beginning.
